- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a 1–2 day lagged smoothing filter to dampen immediate post-spike forecasts.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending upward, model frequently overestimates; cap forecast at 1.2x recent 7-day average to avoid overconfidence.
- In low-sentiment environments, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–3% buffer to forecast for volatility drag.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model exhibits high variance; use median of 3-day rolling forecast instead of 30-day mean to reduce noise.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65), model tends to ignore it; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average of prior 10 days.
- For sentiment > 0.3, model often overestimates upward momentum; reduce forecast by 3–5% if sentiment > 0.4 and price > 70.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop; add 1–2% downward adjustment to forecast if sentiment < 0.1 and price < 65.
